result.title: Evaluating Video LLMs' Understanding of Corner Cases in Autonomous Driving
result.summary: Natural language explanations promised by modern Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) offer autonomous driving systems a path toward detailed scene description and interpretable decision making on the road. While recent benchmarks have begun assessing these models on driving scenes, they mainly target routine traffic conditions and general comprehension tasks based on existing driving datasets and therefore fail to evaluate model performance on the rarest and most safety-critical driving events, also known as "corner cases". To provide a comprehensive evaluation of Video LLMs on precisely these scenarios, we introduce DashBench, a benchmark testing 25 Video LLMs on 1,709 carefully curated driving videos spanning not only collision-related corner cases but also rare non-collision ones. Through extensive prompts and open-ended question answering, we expose a critical capability gap: all evaluated models perform substantially below the threshold required for safety-critical driving applications, frequently misjudging or missing dangerous events on the road ahead and hallucinating non-existent agents or actions in their explanations. We believe DashBench, combining an extensive dataset with a rigorous evaluation toolkit and a detailed diagnosis of current model limitations, drives progress toward safer, more explainable autonomous driving systems. The code and data will be shared at: cornercase-dashbench.github.io

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DashBench，一个面向自动驾驶极端场景的 Video LLM 评测基准：整理 1,709 段视频，覆盖碰撞与罕见非碰撞事件，以开放式问答测试 25 个模型，并给出能力诊断。
AI.relevance_reason: 其诊断出的漏判前方危险事件与虚构不存在实体，可作为核查 VLM 是否真正使用视觉证据、保留任务必要细节的失败参照，但论文不涉及 latent 状态生成或训练，联系限于评测与失败分析。
